name: WEDCO
old_description: This year, we proudly celebrate 75 years of delivering trusted solutions! Since 1950, WEDCO has been built on strong relationships and dedicated leadership. We’re especially grateful to the Elmore Family, whose vision and commitment guided us for decades. In 2008, we began transitioning ownership from the Elmores, and today, we’re proudly 100% employee-owned.
about:
WEDCO is headquartered in Reno, Nevada, with additional locations in Fallon, Carson City, and Winnemucca. The company was founded in 1950 and operated for decades under the leadership of the Elmore family. In 2008, ownership began transitioning from the Elmores, and today WEDCO is 100 percent employee-owned.

The company functions as an electrical distributor and solutions partner, maintaining over $10 million in inventory across its four Northern Nevada branches. It supplies products from brands such as Square D, Schneider Electric, Milwaukee Tool, Southwire, and Eaton, covering panelboards, load centers, push buttons, drives, soft starters, surge protection, and safety switches. In addition to product distribution, WEDCO provides VFD programming and start-up services, motor control training, project management, switchgear and lighting quotations, and general technical training.

WEDCO serves industrial pump contractors, residential and commercial electrical contractors, industrial automation and MRO customers, mining operations, and utility companies throughout Northern Nevada. Its customer base includes contractors and end users who rely on local stock and technical support for electrical infrastructure projects.

The company emphasizes its employee-ownership model and long-standing community ties — including support for the University of Nevada, youth sports, and the Boys & Girls Club — as factors that align its incentives with customer outcomes and regional economic health.

about:
Wagner's Fabrication is a family-owned and operated welding and metal fabrication shop based in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The company has been serving the region since 1988.

The shop specializes in precision TIG welding for medical and aerospace applications, as well as custom metal fabrication. It handles projects ranging from small individual jobs to large-scale aerospace and medical welding contracts. The facility's combined team experience exceeds 50 years.

Wagner's Fabrication serves the medical device and aerospace industries, along with general industrial and individual clients. Examples of work include precision medical welding, precision aerospace welding, and custom fabrication projects such as stainless exhaust systems, motorcycle repairs, and magnesium engine cases.

The company emphasizes a detailed, project-specific approach rather than standardized production, positioning itself as an alternative to larger, less flexible welding providers in the Colorado Springs area.

name: Walker Woodworking | Manufacturing Plant
old_description: Since 2000, Walker Woodworking has established a reputation for quality craftsmanship, exceptional service, and a commitment to providing the finest materials, the latest innovations, and the best cabinet designs for your home or business. When you choose our custom cabinets, you have access to a range of options that other cabinet makers cannot offer.
about:
Walker Woodworking operates from a 75,000-square-foot facility in Shelby, North Carolina. The company was incorporated in 2000 by Travis Walker, a former paramedic who began woodworking as a hobby in the 1990s. After borrowing $3,000 from his grandmother for tools in 1996, he worked from his aunt’s garage and his father-in-law’s shop before opening a 2,100-square-foot plant. His wife, Stacey, joined as a full-time partner in 2006, and the business remains family-owned.

The shop produces custom and semi-custom cabinetry for kitchens, bathrooms, entertainment centers, and built-ins, along with cabinet lighting routing and extrusion preparation for aluminum extrusions. In-house engineers, artisans, and craftsmen — 32 strong as of the latest update — handle design, machining, assembly, and installation of lighting components. The facility replaced a 10,000-square-foot building in 2021, following six earlier expansions.

Walker Woodworking serves homeowners, interior designers, and builders across the region. Its showroom, Greenbrook Design Center, opened in 2018 in downtown Shelby, provides a space for clients to review materials and designs. The company had completed over 400 kitchen projects by 2012 and continues to serve both residential and light commercial projects.

The founders’ original passion — turning a grandfather’s red oak into heirloom pieces — still drives the operation. The company emphasizes locally handcrafted work, a no-cookie-cutter approach, and community-focused values. Strategic growth, including the 2021 facility relocation, was pursued to maintain personalized service and quick adaptation to client needs.

about:
Walt Palmer Supply, Inc. operates from Salt Lake City, Utah, where it was founded in 1958. The business remains under second-generation family ownership, continuing a legacy of serving local supply houses, contractors, and homeowners across the state.

The company runs a manufacturing facility focused on sheet metal fabrication. Its product lines include HVAC square and round ducts designed for efficient airflow, plumbing supplies such as water heater pans and venting components, and a range of roofing metalwork — jacks, flashings, curbs, and caps. A custom design service allows for tailored sheet metal solutions beyond the standard catalog.

Primary customers are Utah-based wholesale supply houses, mechanical and roofing contractors, and residential homeowners. The company positions its HVAC, plumbing, and roofing components for both commercial and residential construction projects throughout the region.

Walt Palmer Supply emphasizes a commitment to quality and on-time delivery rooted in its family-owned tradition. The firm states that its manufacturing approach prioritizes durability and ease of installation across its ductwork, plumbing, and roofing lines.

name: Wapsie Valley Creamery
old_description: Wapsie has successfully produced products in the dairy industry since 1906.  Although the dairy industry has shown little growth over the years, Wapsie has continuously adjusted its manufacturing processes and equipment to compete in the volatile landscapes of the dairy industry.  Wapsie Valley Creamery continues to invest in new equipment that is able to process more milk more efficiently to obtain the best yields in its products.  Although the company has grown over the years, the company is still a relatively small company in the dairy industry.
about:
Wapsie Valley Creamery, a family-owned dairy processor, has operated in Independence, Iowa since 1906. The company began as a local creamery and remains under family ownership.

The company manufactures cheese, lactose, and whey products at its Independence processing plant, sourcing raw milk from over 170 independent dairy farms across eastern Iowa, southwestern Wisconsin, and northwestern Illinois. A workforce of approximately 140 employees runs the facility, which has continuously updated its manufacturing processes and equipment to handle larger milk volumes and improve product yields.

Cheese is sold to large wholesale companies that cut and shred it into private-label packages for retail distribution. Lactose goes to food manufacturers for use in confectionery, sweeteners, and dairy blends. Reduced-lactose whey is supplied to wholesalers for processed cheese, cheese spreads, and calf milk replacer.

Wapsie Valley Creamery states that its point of difference is a commitment to surpass normal quality standards. The plant operates under inspection by the USDA, FDA, and state agencies, maintains an on-site quality assurance laboratory, and uses outside labs for pathogen testing, while ongoing equipment upgrades aim to boost processing efficiency.

name: Ward's Manufacturing
old_description: Founded by siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward, the company is committed to domestic manufacturing and building long-term partnerships by delivering high-quality, made-in-USA parts with unmatched flexibility.
about:
Ward's Manufacturing operates from Warren, Rhode Island, where siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward founded the company in 2022. The brother‑sister team, both former buyers of fabrication services, launched the shop after experiencing the difficulties of sourcing reliable domestic metalwork. Their family background includes a grandfather who was a carpenter rebuilding post‑war London and another who worked as an auto mechanic and metalworker, instilling a service‑oriented trade ethic. The business is certified as a woman‑owned small business.

The shop provides fiber laser cutting (3 kW, 5 × 10 ft bed, ±0.001″ cut tolerance), CNC press brake bending (190‑ton, up to 10 ft length), machining (thread cutting, countersinking, counterboring, reaming, inserts, laser etching), and in‑house finishing (#4 brushed, vibratory tumbling, glass bead blasting, orbital sanding). Product design and engineering support covers CAD creation from sketches, design optimization, and GD&T expertise. Value‑added services include powder coating, wet painting, anodizing, assembly, welding, and a range of surface treatments. There is no minimum order quantity; the company runs from single prototypes to production runs of tens of thousands of units and has shipped to 43 U.S. states and four Canadian provinces.

Customers span aerospace and defense, marine and boat building, robotics and automation, electronics and enclosure fabrication, renewable energy (wind turbine and solar components), medical devices, industrial equipment, automotive, and niche sectors such as shellfish aquaculture, art, and custom signage. The client base consists mainly of small‑to‑mid‑sized OEMs and manufacturers across North America who require tight tolerances and fast turnaround.

Ward's differentiates itself with a 99 % quality rate, domestic production in Warren, and a collaborative approach that includes expedited 24‑ to 48‑hour rush delivery, no minimum orders, and woman‑owned/green‑manufacturer certifications that help clients meet supplier‑diversity and sustainability goals.

name: Warwick Mills Inc
old_description: Warwick specializes in weaving high-strength polyester, nylon, and polypropylene fibers. We are also experts in adhesion, using custom RFL and isocyanate formulas to bond textiles and rubber based upon your application's individual requirements.
about:
Warwick Mills operates from New Ipswich, New Hampshire, where it has built a 135-plus-year history in fabric engineering. Ownership details are not disclosed in available sources.

The company engineers technical textiles, custom adhesives, and performance coatings, taking projects from research and development through testing to full-scale manufacturing. Core processes include high-strength weaving of polyester, nylon, and polypropylene fibers, textile lamination, and the formulation of RFL and isocyanate adhesives for bonding textiles to rubber. Warwick produces custom roll goods such as fabric laminates, chemical-biological barriers, materials for inflatable structures, and flexible composites, including its TurtleSkin puncture-resistant fabrics.

Warwick serves safety, aerospace, and outdoor markets, with a documented partnership supplying lightweight, puncture-resistant TurtleSkin material to Bohle for integration into Schwalbe professional bicycle tires. Its customer base includes original equipment manufacturers seeking protective textile solutions for demanding applications.

The company emphasizes an integrated development-and-manufacturing model, designing with production in mind to shorten lead times. Its cooperative development philosophy fosters active exchange with customers, and its ISO 9001:2015 certification underscores a stated commitment to quality.

name: Waukesha-Pearce Industries (WPI)
old_description: Waukesha-Pearce Industries is a custom manufacturer and distributor of power generation equipment and parts, including low- and medium-voltage switchgear. Serves utility and industrial power generation markets; offers repair and maintenance of switchgear.
about:
Waukesha-Pearce Industries (WPI) is headquartered in Bakersfield, California, and traces its roots to 1924 when Louis Pearce Sr. founded the company on a vision of caring for employees and customers to earn their loyalty. Now in its fourth generation of family ownership, the business has grown from a local enterprise into a multi-location operation serving the western United States.

The company operates as a custom manufacturer and distributor of power generation equipment, producing low- and medium-voltage switchgear alongside generator accessories and parts. It also represents brands in construction, mining, and engine-driven compression and drilling equipment. WPI provides field and shop services, preventive maintenance, real-time fleet telematics, undercarriage repair, welding and fabrication, and build-to-suit power generation systems through its Build-to-Suit PowerGen™ offering. With 200–499 employees across multiple locations, the company handles both equipment sales and full-lifecycle support.

WPI serves utilities, industrial plants, oil and gas operators, construction contractors, and mining companies. Its power generation customers include standby and prime power installations, while its construction and mining division supports fleets with parts, service, and telematics. The engine division supplies compression and onshore drilling support equipment for energy-sector clients.

The company emphasizes its four-generation family legacy and a culture built on core values established by its founder. It positions its combination of people, parts, and equipment as a differentiator for keeping customer operations moving.

about:
Founded in 1910 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Wayne Mills is a family-owned textile manufacturer now in its fifth generation. The company began weaving twill tapes, bindings, and light webbings at a time when steam was produced from coal and yarn arrived by horse and wagon.

Today the firm operates a 150,000-square-foot complex of nine buildings on four acres in a historic Philadelphia district. A workforce of more than 60 runs warping and weaving machines, a high-speed bleaching range, and an on-site dyehouse equipped with 16 skein dyeing machines and a computer-controlled Mageba continuous dye range. The facility also houses finishing, coating, lamination, and custom cutting and packaging lines. Stock items such as cotton tapes (styles 6210, 5541, 5526, 4214, 5533) and polyester and nylon webbings are kept on hand for rapid shipment.

Wayne Mills serves apparel, bindings, military-specification, and bag-and-strap markets. Customers include brands such as Analog Watch Company and government-related buyers; the company's military-specification webbings meet defense requirements. Its textile design service helps clients develop custom narrow fabrics from concept to production.

The company emphasizes small dye-lot minimums of just 15 pounds—far below the industry standard of 500–1,000 pounds—fast turnaround enabled by large inventory, and a tenured team averaging 25-plus years of service. Environmental recognition from the City of Philadelphia for wastewater treatment and membership in the Narrow Fabric Institute underscore its operational standards. All products are manufactured in the USA.
